chapter: Touring, Ella Fitzgerald and South America
title: Staying in Buenos Aires and discovering tango
summary: After the tour he stayed in Buenos Aires, heard tango and Piazzolla, and found it seeped into his music.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you stay in South America after the tour or did you…?
I did, yeah. I stayed in Buenos Aires. I borrowed, I don’t know, two or three hundred bucks from Norman Granz and I stayed in, on… not, not terribly long afterwards.

Well, I had gotten to know some people, I guess, and I was fascinated by the music. I heard tango music. I heard Astor Piazzolla. I heard his music. I may have met him there. And there was another guy whose nickname was (Pachuko?). I’ll think of his real name. Anyway, I go to this place where this tango music was playing. I couldn’t believe it. I hadn’t heard… you know, you hear the real stuff and the difference between that and the Brazilian music. It was, it was quite an experience. I really loved it.
When you came home with all this new sound in your head, what did you do with it?
(laughs) Did you incorporate all of that in, soon after or…?

Well, I don’t know if I did consciously or not, but I’m sure that it seeped in there just like my discovering Béla Bartók in music school (laughs) did, you know. I assume that one’s experience with any luck… I’m looking at a picture of Zoot Sims as we talked. (laughs) It was a great experience. And Scott Colley and I played in Buenos Aires just a few years ago and a couple that had owned a club where I used to go to… they, they came in to the concert. It was really nice.
